item.title: Designation
item.description:
Office of the Mayor | Special Materials | Notice | Flagged: Special Materials (non-routine) In plain English (machine-written): The Office of the Mayor designated New York City Tourism + Conventions to develop a cultural passport program encouraging visits to participating sites in each borough, and the Department of Records and Information Services to publish online biographical information about past laws that renamed streets or parks, both under Local Laws 110 and 122 of 2026.

November 9, 2026

 

I hereby designate New York City Tourism + Conventions as the designated agency pursuant to and for the purposes of section 3-119.13 of the Administrative Code of the City of New York as enacted by Local Law 110 of 2026, a Local Law in relation to requiring a designated agency to develop and implement a cultural passport program encouraging visitation to participating sites in each borough.

I further designate the Department of Records and Information Services as the designated agency pursuant to and for the purposes of subdivision c of section 25-102.2 of the Administrative Code of the City of New York as enacted by Local Law 122 of 2026, a Local Law in relation to the online publication of new biographical information relating to past local laws that changed the name of streets or parks.

item.description:
Health and Mental Hygiene | Procurement | Intent to Award | Due: 2026-11-30 | Flagged: Contract value ≥ $1M In plain English (machine-written): The Department of Health and Mental Hygiene plans to award a nine-year, $11,053,955 contract without open competition to The Jericho Project, starting Jan. 1, 2027, to provide housing and support services for young adults or parents in supportive housing.

Pursuant to Section 3-04(b)(2)(ii) of the Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules, the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) intends to enter into a Negotiated Acquisition with The Jericho Project to provide housing and support services for young adult individuals or parents in a congregate supportive housing setting.

Competitive Sealed Bidding or Competitive Sealed Proposals are neither practical nor advantageous due to the limited number of vendors available and qualified to perform these specialized services, as evidenced by the Human Resources Administration (HRA) RFP (EPIN 09617I0006). This open-ended RFP remains open because the City is attempting to increase supportive housing stock. Because the HRA RFP remains open, DOHMH does not anticipate receiving alternative expressions of interest for current supporting housing units.

The Jericho Project has demonstrated satisfactory performance. The proposed contract term is for 9 years, with an anticipated start date of January 1, 2027, and a total procurement value of $11,053,955.00

This notice is for informational purposes only.
